back: A repeatable reproduce-and-measure engine run on half a dozen recent agent-reliability and interpretability papers — each an honest, pre-registered, judge-free measurement, nulls reported as headlines.
Wilson = honest error bar on one proportion (sane at small N and 0%/100%). Newcombe = honest error bar on the gap between two; includes zero → report a null.
It is self-graded homework — sweet-talkable, not reproducible. Deterministic oracles trade subtlety for a verdict any skeptic can re-run.
The stated scope: mechanical reliability of small models under a hard budget, disclosed everywhere. A deliberate choice, not a limitation.
For every project, without notes: (1) 60-second pitch, (2) defend the caveat unprompted, (3) re-derive the headline number + its interval, (4) answer the top skeptic probe.
Lead with dim-stage: the deepest, a bitwise-validated instrument, and a pre-registered null answered on the paper's own open question about small models.
Published paper → rebuild or reuse the harness → iterate a metric under verification → publish openly, with unusual statistical honesty at a scale one person can own every number.
